module_title: MS Excel - Foundational Basics, Cells, and Formulas
introduction: In the 'Computer Knowledge' section of SSC CGL, MS Excel is an extremely critical 'Spreadsheet' application. It is used to organize data into tables (rows and columns) and perform mathematical calculations. At this foundational level, we will focus on the grid architecture and the absolute basic rules of writing formulas.

core_concepts.title: Rows, Columns, and Cells
core_concepts.description:
An Excel worksheet is a massive grid.
- Columns: These are the vertical pillars, identified by Alphabets (A, B, C...).
- Rows: These are the horizontal lines, identified by Numbers (1, 2, 3...).
- Cell: The fundamental box where a row and a column intersect. (e.g., Column A and Row 1 intersect to form cell 'A1').

core_concepts.title: Active Cell & Name Box
core_concepts.description: The specific cell you have currently clicked on (highlighted with a thick green border) is called the 'Active Cell'. The exact address/name of this active cell is always displayed in the 'Name Box' located at the top-left corner of the screen (e.g., C4).

core_concepts.title: The Golden Rule of Formulas (The '=' Sign)
core_concepts.description: This is the most important rule in Excel: Every single formula or function MUST begin with an 'Equals to' sign (`=`). If you type a calculation without the `=` sign (like `5+5`), Excel will treat it as normal text and will NOT calculate the answer.

core_concepts.title: Basic Mathematical Operators
core_concepts.description:
Excel uses specific symbols for basic math:
- Addition: `+`
- Subtraction: `-`
- Multiplication: `*` (Asterisk)
- Division: `/` (Forward slash)

important_entities.name: File Extension
important_entities.significance: From Excel 2007 onwards, the default file extension is `.xlsx` (prior to 2003, it was `.xls`). An entire Excel file is officially called a 'Workbook'.

important_entities.name: Default Worksheets
important_entities.significance: In older versions (2003-2010), opening a new Workbook gave you 3 blank worksheets by default (Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3). In modern Excel (2013 onwards), it defaults to only 1 blank worksheet.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common Tier-1 question asks for the correct format of a cell address. Remember: The Column ALPHABET always comes first, followed by the Row NUMBER. Therefore, 'A1' is correct. '1A' is completely invalid.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: C for Column, C for Characters
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember which is which: Columns are represented by Characters (Alphabets). Rows are numbers.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct questions like 'Which symbol is used to initiate a formula in Excel?' are guaranteed staples. Always choose the equals sign (=).
